dossier.architecture: Twin turrets over dual conical spindexers, with extensible net hopper and L1 climb.

subsystems.drivetrain: Swerve; exact module variant unresolved here.
subsystems.intake: Intake deploy also expands hopper; commanded roller speed follows chassis speed and collector motion agitates fuel.
subsystems.transfer: Spinning floors and ribbed cones drive two uptake ramps. Bristles → stacked wheels → shaped cones after inadequate feed and jams.
subsystems.scoring: Independent turret aiming and hood control; aluminum flywheels replaced overly heavy steel trial. Separate kickers control fuel entering each shooter.
subsystems.endgame: L1 chosen for weight and autonomous speed; physical lift details not completely established by interview.
subsystems.controls: Each turret has offset-corrected hub vector, interpolation and moving-shot calculation. Three Limelight 4s fuse with odometry; can shoot during climb.

versions: First regional used stacked wheels; cone/rib geometry revised afterward.
Steel flywheel trial was rejected, not final hardware.
dossier.analysis: Dual turrets trade feed complexity and mass for multiple heading-independent streams. Their value depends on both streams remaining supplied during real congestion and on the measured benefit over a simpler single turret or drum.
limits: Only the reviewed published configurations are established; intermediate changes may be undocumented.

context_documents.title: 2026-1706 · Twin spindexers trade packaging freedom for multiple coupled interfaces
context_documents.body:
# 2026-1706: Twin spindexers trade packaging freedom for multiple coupled interfaces

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

## Published / retained construction account

The mechanism has two rotating floor/cone systems and uptake ramps, separately controlled kickers, independent turrets and hood adjustment. The interview describes X44-driven indexer systems, 6-inch aluminum flywheels replacing heavy steel trials, an under-mounted battery on a pinned removable panel, and chassis-speed-dependent intake voltage bounded around 6.5–12 V.

## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

Aluminum flywheels were chosen after the steel trial proved too heavy. The battery mounting responds to crowded internal packaging. The retained interview account describes bristles, stacked wheels and shaped cones as successive feed iterations.

## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

Two aiming channels do not automatically double match output. Fuel must be distributed to both cones, delivered through both ramps and accelerated without one path starving or overpacking. Moving-shot math must use the location of each turret rather than a single robot-center vector; angular chassis motion creates different local velocities at separated release points. Dynamic collector speed can match acquisition to chassis motion, but the exact speed signal and interpolation should be checked in code because the caption wording mixes angular and translational quantities. The removable battery panel is part of the architecture: dense packaging is only useful if the robot can still be serviced reliably.

## Proposed validation — not performed

Test unequal hopper loading, one jammed lane, low battery, turning shots and underbody battery retention after bump contact. Verify the actual intake-speed input in source code before reproducing the controller.

## Limits

Focused technical passages and the retained dossier are the evidence scope. Exact event installation, complete CAD tolerances and all intermediate revisions are not certified.

## Sources and navigation

- [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=O2KMy1tlU9M](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=O2KMy1tlU9M)

source_reviews.title: Ratchet Rockers Mirage championship release
source_reviews.review_basis: Read the team release and written responses in the public thread.
source_reviews.facts: Both turrets use two CANcoders, the cable carriers have a four-pound constant-force return, front and rear shooter rollers run at different speeds, and the A-bot shooters had a strict 12-inch envelope. The sloped intake plate addressed fuel trapped during retraction.
source_reviews.limitations: The release comments give design intent and fixes. They do not specify the complete spindexer roller geometry or shooter control maps.

source_reviews.title: Mirage offseason B-bot discussion
source_reviews.review_basis: Read the public thread’s October continuation and team comparisons.
source_reviews.facts: Team reports 14-inch B-bot turret envelopes, roughly 84 fuel in the B-bot hopper, and roughly 12–13 versus 11–12 BPS for A and B respectively. It documents breaking in a tighter printed turret gear.
source_reviews.limitations: Reported rates lack fill, battery and test protocols. Keep B-bot claims separate from the championship configuration.

source_review.whole_robot_explanation: Mirage packages two independently rotating shooters over twin indexing paths. The team protected the space for indexing with Thrifty Narrow swerve modules and treated each 12-inch A-bot shooter cylinder as a firm boundary. The resulting integration problem spans power transmission, cable travel and repeatable absolute angle sensing on both shooters. The published comparison with the B bot provides an example of what changed when the package was relaxed.
source_review.piece_flow: Fuel crosses the bumper at the front intake and reaches the twin spindexer region through a sloped transition. The indexing assembly supplies the two shooter paths. At each launch module the front wheel and rear accelerator wheels have different commanded mechanical speed relationships through their transmission. The release establishes that topology, with insufficient detail to assign a final cone construction, compression, or loaded delivery rate to each branch.
source_review.packaging_and_motion: The narrower modules redistribute drivetrain bulk away from the spindexer. The team allowed slight contact between the intake plates and bumper foam to preserve edge distance at holes. A remnant telescoping tube served as a stiffener for the Limelight mount in the released configuration. Its presence alone provides no basis for assigning a climb level to that version.

subsystems.name: Intake and stow transition
subsystems.construction: Sloped plate between front intake and indexing region. Bumpers use formed 1/8-inch 5052-H32 backing stock with holes on a one-inch pattern, PE foam and a sewn cover.
subsystems.operation: The transition guides fuel out of the pinch region while the intake pulls in. Local foam displacement permits the mechanism to travel past the bumper edge.
subsystems.team_rationale: Fuel formerly lodged below the transition, dented the spindexer wall and prevented retraction. Iterating the plate substantially improved the behavior.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Evaluate stow with fuel deliberately left at the interface, including dented walls and aged foam. Clearance measured with an empty robot can miss this failure.
subsystems.interfaces: Intake plate to foam, mounting holes to edge, slope to spindexer wall.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Inspect for a fresh witness mark or dent and check that repair foam has comparable compliance. The team’s alternative XPE was still under evaluation.
subsystems.unknowns: Plate angle, roller transmission and allowable interference.

subsystems.name: Twin launch modules and turret services
subsystems.construction: Two turret assemblies, dual CANcoders on each, and spring-retracted cable chains running through blue pulleys. Shooter drivetrain preserves distinct speeds and rotation directions for front and rear rollers.
subsystems.operation: The team describes residue-based angle reconstruction using the Chinese remainder method. The spring takes up returning cable carrier during rotation.
subsystems.team_rationale: Fit the complete path in a 12-inch A-bot cylinder while preserving the fuel path and speed relationships.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: The two angle signals extend the uniquely measurable range if their ratios and offsets are suitable. Offset consistency after service and cable reaction torque under motion matter to repeatability.
subsystems.interfaces: Fuel entrance to accelerator rollers, encoder gearing to azimuth estimate, and fixed wiring to moving carrier.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Inspect cable tracking over full permitted travel and compare both raw absolute angles after a repair. Belt and shaft alignment were cited as possible contributors to B-bot behavior.
subsystems.unknowns: Encoder tooth counts, sensor reconciliation, cable travel limits and actual hood calibration.

revisions: For Champs the team iterated the sloped intake plate. The offseason B bot had larger turrets and a tight printed 8-DP spur gear. It was broken in at reduced speed until reported current dropped to roughly 10–15 A maximum, then greased. The team estimated a three- to fourfold reduction in backlash versus A bot.
transferable_principles: Budget motor, belt, wiring and sensor envelopes inside every duplicated turret. Compare shooter accuracy and feed balance together, since doubling the launch modules doubles potential paths without establishing equal supply.
disconfirming_conditions: The twin layout loses its advantage if one stream frequently starves, cable travel constrains the useful aim range, or a single launcher clears match loads faster after accounting for alignment and outages.
remaining_gaps: Final intake and spindexer assembly details, including the exact split between shared circulation and independent uptake, branch rates, climb installation by event and the deployed shot solver remain open. The public interview caption request returned HTTP 429 and supplied no evidence.
